Think being Homeland Security secretary is tough? Well, it’s nothing compared to the struggles of trying to be a “good uncle.”

Markwayne Mullin tried to make that case to Congress during Wednesday’s House Homeland Security Committee hearing on global threats but, sadly for him, received little sympathy from the reps or on social media.

Mullin is currently under fire for using a government plane to fly to the LSU-Texas college football game on Saturday, one day after plane departures were halted nationwide, causing massive travel disruptions across the country.

Although the stoppage had been lifted before Mullin’s flight, thousands of flights had been canceled, and many people were forced to scramble for alternative travel options even as the secretary flew to the game.

Mullin initially justified the trip to CNBC on Tuesday, saying his job requires him to fly on government planes.

“We would have never went if the airways weren’t completely open,” he insisted. “They’d been completely open for 21 hours.”

Mullin offered another reason on Wednesday that seems similar to the one Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) gave in February 2021, when he ditched Texas during record cold temperatures for the warmer climate of Cancun, Mexico.

Cruz initially blamed his daughters, saying they asked to go away with friends since there was no power and school was out, and he just “wanted to be a good dad.”

Mullin told the House Homeland Security Hearing on Wednesday that he took his family and great-nieces to an LSU game he claimed was scheduled for weeks before “because I wanted to be a good uncle and take my little niece who’s never been to an LSU game and she’s a huge LSU fan, to a game.”

Mullin admitted he discussed canceling the trip on Saturday morning.

“We had deep conversations about it, and it came down to the fact that if we canceled something with the airspace completely open, it could bring confusion because I was meeting the governor there, I was meeting other people there, that it would show distrust that we’re not even willing to fly.”

He also insisted that he paid for the game tickets.

Mullin’s emphatic desire to be a good uncle may have won him points with his relatives, but not so much on social media.
